subject: How to resize axis and legend text?

messages.author: ada445e3a439dd38
messages.subject: How to resize axis and legend text?
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to increase the size of the axes and the labels with a
simple parameter setup. The default is really small for a two column
paper layout. I am using:

theme_bw( base_size=20 )

It works as expected. However text is being printed outside of the PDF
canvas, more specifically it is being cropped on the right side.

How should I handle this?

Thanks in advance,
--
Sérgio Nunes

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: How to resize axis and legend text?
parts:
Hi,

I don't know about the cropping (could you post a minimal example to
demonstrate this?) but I'm surprised you'd use a font of 20 for a
paper. For a two column layout, I would typically save a 4-inch wide
figure with ggsave(..., width=4), keeping the font size to 10. Are you
maybe resizing the plot when you insert it in your document?

Best,

baptiste

messages.author: ada445e3a439dd38
messages.subject: Re: How to resize axis and legend text?
parts:
Thanks for the quick reply. I really appreciate it given my looming
deadline for this paper.
My procedure is the following:

In R, I prepare the PDFs using pdf("figs.pdf", width = 16, height = 9)
and then using ggplot or qplot with theme_bw( base_size=20 ) I plot
each chart. Given the nature of my figures, I tend to prefer this
"landscape" view.

In LaTeX, I simply include the figures with:

\begin{figure}
\centering
\includegraphics[page=13,width=0.9\columnwidth]{../plots/figs.pdf}
\end{figure}

I placed a PDF evidencing the problem here:
http://irlab.fe.up.pt/sandbox/cropped.pdf

Thanks again,
--
Sérgio Nunes

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: How to resize axis and legend text?
parts:
My personal preference is to never let LaTeX resize the picture,
otherwise the font size is never really consistent in the document. In
this spirit I might also suggest the tikzDevice package, where LaTeX
actually processes the text itself in the figure so that its size
always matches the rest of the document. You'd have to create separate
files for each figure though.

Is there a particular reason you want a graphic of 16x9 inches and
not, say, 4x2.2?

Best,

baptiste
